methodologyNotes: Specs sourced primarily from official manufacturer product pages (tp-link.com, eero.com, netgear.com, techspecs.ui.com) and corroborated via Wikipedia, smallnetbuilder.com, Tom's Hardware, and Dong Knows Tech reviews. The ASUS website (asus.com) persistently geo-redirects to the German homepage for all regional variants, blocking access to spec pages; ASUS product specs (RT-AX88U Pro, ZenWiFi BT8) were therefore verified against official ASUS tech-spec pages where reachable plus multiple independent reviews and US retailer listings (Amazon, Best Buy, Micro Center, Newegg). ADVERSARIAL REVISION 2026-06-17: corrected several fabricated/incorrect entries -- (1) ASUS RT-AX88U Pro was wrongly listed as AX7800/7800 Mbps with an 8x1G/2xUSB port layout and a dual-core 1.8 GHz Broadcom CPU; it is AX6000 (1148+4804), 2x2.5G + 4x1G + 1xUSB3.0, 2.0 GHz quad-core, released Jan 2023. (2) 'ASUS ZenWiFi Pro BT8' does not exist; the real product is the ZenWiFi BT8 (BE14000, dual 2.5G ports, 5,900 sq ft 2-pack) -- the prior BE25000/10G-port specs belong to the higher-tier ZenWiFi BT10. (3) Ubiquiti UniFi Express bands/ports/CPU were wrong (actual 573.5+2402 Mbps, dual 1 GbE ports, dual-core A53). (4) Netgear RAXE500 USB count corrected to 2x USB 3.0. (5) eero Max 7 release corrected to 2023. Google Nest Wifi Pro (Qualcomm IPQ5018, AXE5400, 2x1G, 2,200 sq ft) confirmed via Wikipedia and Qualcomm. Netgear Orbi RBKE963 confirmed via netgear.com/B&H. eero products confirmed via eero.com shop pages. TP-Link products confirmed via tp-link.com product pages (Archer AXE75 reflects V2 hardware with a 2.5G port). priceUsd = US MSRP or starting retail price for base/reference config. All sources accessed 2026-06-15. Numbers are plain (no units in value). A null beats any guess.
